github.title: GitHub
github.setupHint: Create a GitHub App, then paste the credentials here.
github.appDescription: Create a GitHub App for your instance. Allows repo access across orgs without a personal token.
github.credentialsUnreadableHint: The stored private key cannot be decrypted. Continue on GitHub to configure a new App and replace the local configuration.
github.credentialsNeedAttentionHint: Ploydok cannot decrypt the stored private key. Continue on GitHub to configure a new App. Its credentials will replace the local configuration when you return. The existing GitHub App will not be deleted.
github.resetLocalHint: This deletes the unreadable GitHub App configuration from Ploydok only. It does not uninstall or delete the App on GitHub, and it does not modify any GitHub installation. You must manage the existing App and its installations manually on GitHub.
github.connectedHint: This account can import repositories through the Ploydok GitHub App.
github.needsLink: An instance administrator must link a GitHub account or organization before you can import repositories.
github.needsAdmin: An instance administrator must configure the GitHub App before you can connect.
github.installationsHintAdmin: Accounts and organizations where the Ploydok GitHub App is installed. Revoking removes the App from that GitHub account or organization.
github.installationsHintMember: Accounts and organizations where the Ploydok GitHub App is installed. Disconnecting removes only your local Ploydok link. An instance administrator must add new accounts or organizations.
github.installedUpdated: GitHub App installation #{{id}} updated. Your repositories are syncing below.
github.installedReceived: GitHub App installation #{{id}} received. Your repositories are syncing below.
github.verifyCredentialsFailed: Failed to verify GitHub App credentials: {{message}}
github.revokeHint: This uninstalls the Ploydok GitHub App from @{{login}} on GitHub and removes its repository access.
github.disconnectHint: This removes your local Ploydok link to @{{login}}. It does not uninstall the App or change any installation on GitHub.
github.emptyInstallations: The GitHub App is configured but has no repository access yet. Install it on a GitHub account or organization to enable repository import.
github.registeredHint: GitHub App registered. Repository access is managed from the active installations below.
github.resetAppHint: This uninstalls {{name}} from every connected GitHub account or organization and deletes its local Ploydok configuration. The App itself stays registered on GitHub: delete it from the account's Developer settings if you no longer need it. This action cannot be undone.
github.cachedHint: Repos are served from a Postgres cache so the create-app picker opens instantly. Webhooks invalidate it on install / repo events; a background sync re-fills stale data.
github.cachedEmpty: No installation cached yet. Click Sync now to import your GitHub installations and their repositories.
github.reconnectHint: GitHub verifies the private key before replacing the local credentials. Existing installations are preserved and repositories are synchronized.
github.notConfiguredHint: Create a new GitHub App, or reconnect the existing one after a local DB reset.
github.needHelpCredentials: Need help finding the GitHub App credentials?
github.howToReconnectTitle: How to reconnect the GitHub App
github.howToReconnectHint: Open the existing App on GitHub, align its URLs, then generate fresh credentials. Existing secrets and private keys cannot be displayed again by GitHub.
github.guideStep1Body: Use the personal settings page, or open your organization and go to Settings → Developer settings → GitHub Apps.
github.guideStep2Body: Keep OAuth during installation disabled, enable Redirect on update, and use these exact values:
github.localhostHint: GitHub cannot deliver webhooks to localhost. Use the public HTTPS URL of your tunnel or deployed API instead of the local webhook URL above.
github.guideStep3AppId: Copy App ID, Client ID and the App name from General. The slug is the last part of the public App URL: github.com/apps/<slug>.
github.guideStep3Secret: Under Client secrets, generate a new secret and paste it now.
github.guideStep3Key: Under Private keys, generate a key, open the downloaded .pem file and paste its complete contents, including BEGIN/END lines.
github.guideStep3Webhook: If webhooks are active, choose a new webhook secret, save it on GitHub, and paste the same value here.

posture.label: Posture
posture.title: Your account perimeter
posture.intro: Three signals drive access safety: the passkeys you hold, the backup codes in reserve, and the devices currently signed in.
posture.passkeysStrong: Two or more devices can sign in.
posture.passkeysFair: Add a second device as a fallback.
posture.totpStrong: A rotating 6-digit code from your authenticator app is enrolled.
posture.totpWeak: Enroll TOTP to satisfy the second-factor requirement.
posture.backupStrong: Recovery path active if a device is lost.
posture.backupWeak: Generated from the CLI — ask an owner to run ploydok-cli admin-recovery.
posture.sessionsWeak: Review other devices and revoke anything unfamiliar.
